requirements.subject: ent:timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 timer operations ARE the operations listed in table 27 (start, stop, read, running and timeout).
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports a number of timer operations as given in table 27.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-operation
requirements.canonical: A timer operation MAY be used in a testcase, a function and an altstep.
requirements.original: These operations may be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.

ambiguity.issue: 'test cases' is used instead of the keyword-level term 'testcase'; the sentence does not mention the module control function, although clause 23.1 states that control components maintain timer lists, so it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive.
readings: A timer operation MAY be used only in a testcase, a function or an altstep.
A timer operation MAY be used in a testcase, a function, an altstep and the module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:any-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `any port` notation MAY be used with the `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check` operations (e.g. `any port.receive`).
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, catch, check); All with ports: yes; Col4: any port.receive

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all port` notation SHALL NOT be used with the `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check` operations.
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, catch, check); All with ports: yes; Col4: any port.receive

requirements.subject: ent:any-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `any` and `all` keywords SHALL NOT be used with ports in the `connect` and `map` operations.
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: connect / map

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all port` notation MAY be used with the `disconnect` and `unmap` operations (e.g. `unmap(self : all port)`).
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: disconnect / unmap; Col3: yes; Col4: unmap(self : all port)

requirements.subject: ent:any-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `any port` notation SHALL NOT be used with the `disconnect` and `unmap` operations.
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: disconnect / unmap; Col3: yes; Col4: unmap(self : all port)

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all port` notation MAY be used with the port `start`, `stop`, `clear` and `halt` operations (e.g. `all port.start`).
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: start, stop, clear, halt; Col3: yes; Col4: all port.start

requirements.subject: ent:any-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `any port` notation SHALL NOT be used with the port `start`, `stop`, `clear` and `halt` operations.
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: start, stop, clear, halt; Col3: yes; Col4: all port.start

requirements.subject: ent:any-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `any port` notation MAY be used with the `checkstate` operation (e.g. `any port.checkstate("Started")`).
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: Checkstate; All with ports: yes; Col3: yes; Col4: any port.checkstate("Started") all port.checkstate("Connected")

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all port` notation MAY be used with the `checkstate` operation (e.g. `all port.checkstate("Connected")`).
requirements.original: Table 26: Any and: Checkstate; All with ports: yes; Col3: yes; Col4: any port.checkstate("Started") all port.checkstate("Connected")

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `start`.
requirements.original: Table 27: Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations: Start timer; Col2: start

requirements.subject: ent:stop-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `stop`.
requirements.original: Table 27: Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations: Stop timer; Col2: stop

requirements.subject: ent:read-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `read`.
requirements.original: Table 27: Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations: Read elapsed time; Col2: read

requirements.subject: ent:running-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `running`.
requirements.original: Table 27: Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations: Check if timer running; Col2: running

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `timeout`.
requirements.original: Table 27: Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations: Timeout event; Col2: timeout

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Each test component and each control component SHALL maintain its own running-timer list (the list of all running timers) and its own timeout-list (the list of all timers that have timed out).
requirements.original: It is assumed that each test component and control component maintain their own running-timers _list and timeout-list,_ i.e. a list of all timers that are actually running and a list of all timers that have timed out.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-list
requirements.canonical: The timeout-list IS part of the snapshot taken during the execution of a testcase.
requirements.original: The timeout-lists are part of the snapshots that are taken when a test case is executed.

ambiguity.issue: 'test case' is used where the TTCN-3 construct 'testcase' (its execution) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:running-timer-list
requirements.canonical: The running-timer list and the timeout-list of a component ARE updated when a timer of the component is started, is stopped or times out, or when the component executes a timeout operation.
requirements.original: The running-timers list and timeout-list are updated if a timer of the component is started, is stopped, times out or the component executes a timeout operation.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool MAY implement the running-timer list and the timeout-list with other data structures, such as a set in which access to timeout events is not restricted by the order of the timeout events.
requirements.original: Other data structures like a set, where the access to timeout events is not restricted by, e.g. the order in which the timeout events have happened, may also be used.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Each test component and control component conceptually maintains exactly one running-timer list and one timeout-list.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Conceptually, each test and control component maintain one running-timers list and one timeout-list only.

requirements.subject: ent:scope-unit
requirements.canonical: Within a scope unit, only timers known in the scope unit (declared in it, passed in as parameters, or known via a runs on clause) CAN be accessed individually.
requirements.original: However, within a given scope unit only timers known in the scope unit can be accessed individually, i.e. timers that are declared in the scope unit, passed in as parameters to the scope unit or known via a runs-on clause.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-operation
requirements.canonical: Stopping timers local to other scope units, or checking whether such timers are running or have timed out, CAN be necessary in special cases, e.g. when re-establishing a test component.
requirements.original: In some special cases (e.g. for re-establishing a test component during a test run), it can be necessary to stop timers local to other scope units or to check if timers local to other scope units are running or have already timed out.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The keywords `all` and `any` CAN be combined with the timer operations `stop`, `timeout` and `running` to address timers local to other scope units.
requirements.original: This can be done by using the keywords all and any in combination with the timer operations stop, timeout and running.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: When a timer expires, the timer IS immediately inactive.
requirements.original: When a timer expires, the timer becomes immediately inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-event
requirements.canonical: When a timer expires, a timeout event IS placed in the timeout-list of the component for which the timer has been declared.
requirements.original: A timeout event is placed in the timeout-list and the timer is removed from the running-timer list of the component for which the timer has been declared.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: When a timer expires, the timer IS removed from the running-timer list of the component for which the timer has been declared.
requirements.original: A timeout event is placed in the timeout-list and the timer is removed from the running-timer list of the component for which the timer has been declared.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-list
requirements.canonical: The timeout-list of the component for which a timer has been declared SHALL NOT contain more than one entry for that timer.
requirements.original: Only one entry for any particular timer may appear in the timeout-list and running-timer list of the component for which the timer has been declared.

requirements.subject: ent:running-timer-list
requirements.canonical: The running-timer list of the component for which a timer has been declared SHALL NOT contain more than one entry for that timer.
requirements.original: Only one entry for any particular timer may appear in the timeout-list and running-timer list of the component for which the timer has been declared.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.condition: the test component is explicitly or implicitly stopped
requirements.canonical: All running timers of a test component SHALL be cancelled automatically when the test component is explicitly or implicitly stopped.
requirements.original: All running timers shall automatically be cancelled when a test component is explicitly or implicitly stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The start timer operation IS used to indicate that a timer shall start running.
requirements.original: The start timer operation is used to indicate that a timer shall start running.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The start timer operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." start [ "(" TimerValue ")" ].
requirements.original: ObjectReference "." start [ "(" ObjectReference ")" ]

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block names the optional parenthesized argument 'ObjectReference' while the restrictions describe a SingleExpression giving the timer value.
readings: The optional argument of the start timer operation IS a SingleExpression giving the timer value.
The optional argument of the start timer operation IS an ObjectReference.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: When a timer is started, the timer IS added to the running-timer list.
requirements.original: When a timer is started, its name is added to the list of running timers (for the given scope unit).

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says the timer is added to the list 'for the given scope unit', while clause 23.1 says each component maintains one running-timer list.
readings: When a timer is started, the timer IS added to the running-timer list of the component.
When a timer is started, the timer IS added to a running-timer list specific to the scope unit.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.condition: no default duration is given in the timer declaration
requirements.canonical: The start timer operation SHALL specify a timer value if the timer declaration gives no default duration.
requirements.original: The optional timer value parameter shall be used if no default duration is given, or if it is desired to override the default value specified in the timer declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The start timer operation MAY specify a timer value to override the default duration given in the timer declaration.
requirements.original: The optional timer value parameter shall be used if no default duration is given, or if it is desired to override the default value specified in the timer declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-value
requirements.canonical: A timer value given in a start timer operation IS applied only to the current instance of the timer.
requirements.original: When a timer duration is overridden, the new value applies only to the current instance of the timer, any later start operations for this timer, which do not specify a duration, shall use the default duration.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: A later start timer operation that does not specify a timer value SHALL use the default duration of the timer.
requirements.original: When a timer duration is overridden, the new value applies only to the current instance of the timer, any later start operations for this timer, which do not specify a duration, shall use the default duration.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: A timer started with the timer value 0.0 times out immediately.
requirements.original: Starting a timer with the timer value 0.0 means that the timer times out immediately.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: Starting a timer with a negative timer value (e.g. resulting from an expression) SHALL cause a runtime error.
requirements.original: Starting a timer with a negative timer value, e.g. the timer value is the result of an expression, or without a specified timer value shall cause a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.condition: no timer value is specified and no default duration exists
requirements.canonical: Starting a timer without a specified timer value SHALL cause a runtime error when the timer has no default duration.
requirements.original: Starting a timer with a negative timer value, e.g. the timer value is the result of an expression, or without a specified timer value shall cause a runtime error.

ambiguity.issue: Read literally, starting a timer 'without a specified timer value' always causes an error, which contradicts the use of the default duration (23.2-s004/s005).
readings: Starting a timer without a timer value SHALL cause a runtime error only if the timer has no default duration.
Starting a timer without a timer value SHALL always cause a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: The timer clock IS running from the float value 0.0 up to the maximum given by the duration.
requirements.original: The timer clock runs from the float value zero (0.0) up to maximum stated by the duration parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The start timer operation MAY be applied to a running timer.
requirements.original: The start operation may be applied to a running timer, in which case the timer is stopped and re-started.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: When the start timer operation is applied to a running timer, the timer IS stopped and re-started.
requirements.original: The start operation may be applied to a running timer, in which case the timer is stopped and re-started.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The start timer operation MAY be applied to a timer that has already expired.
requirements.original: The start operation may be applied to a timer that has already expired; in this case, any entry in the timeout list for this timer shall be removed.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: When the start timer operation is applied to an expired timer, any entry for the timer in the timeout-list SHALL be removed.
requirements.original: The start operation may be applied to a timer that has already expired; in this case, any entry in the timeout list for this timer shall be removed.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-value
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression giving the timer value of a start timer operation SHALL be a non-negative float value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
requirements.original: a) The SingleExpression representing the timer value shall be a non-negative numerical float number (i.e. the value shall be greater than or equal to 0.0; infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.subject: ent:timer-value
requirements.canonical: The timer value of a start timer operation SHALL NOT be `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
requirements.original: a) The SingleExpression representing the timer value shall be a non-negative numerical float number (i.e. the value shall be greater than or equal to 0.0; infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a start timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.
requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.
